# Frozen evaluation fixtures

Committed datasets the skill regression gate scores against.

## `skill_v1.csv`

4000 matches with bookmaker odds and xG, in the football-data.co.uk column layout
`oracle_ingest::data::load_results_csv` reads.

**Provenance.** Generated by `cargo run --release -p oracle-eval --example freeze_fixture` from
`synthetic_history_with_market(4000, 7)`, at the commit that added this file. The example is kept
alongside as executable provenance rather than a prose description that can drift.

**Why this is committed rather than regenerated.** A gate whose dataset comes from calling the
generator would fire whenever the generator changed, which is often — an earlier branch on this repo
moved every synthetic value it produces. The gate could then not distinguish a data change from a
model change, and since data changes are more frequent it would mostly raise false alarms. A gate
that cries wolf gets switched off, so the dataset is frozen and inert: a metric that moves means the
*model* moved.

**Why synthetic rather than real.** Real match data with closing odds is not redistributable here,
and `scripts/fetch-results.sh` downloads it on demand precisely so it need not be committed. A gate
needs a dataset that is present, identical for everyone, and requires no network — which rules the
real data out. This costs the gate nothing it was trying to buy: it detects *regressions*, and it
does not need the absolute skill number to be meaningful in order to notice the number moving.
Absolute skill on real data lives in [`docs/VALIDATION.md`](../../../docs/VALIDATION.md).

**Do not edit this file.** The baseline records its content hash, so an edit invalidates the
comparison rather than quietly moving the bar. To change the dataset, freeze a new `skill_v2.csv`,
point the gate at it, and record a fresh baseline — three visible steps rather than one invisible one.
